conflicts.point: Whether decentralized open-weight distribution improves safety and clinical outcomes through peer audit more effectively than centralized pre-market gatekeeping.

positions.stance: Open-weight distribution enables continuous peer review and adaptation by local practitioners, producing higher adversarial robustness than centralized agency tests.
Open-weight distribution removes compliance records and developer traceability, shifting tort liability onto vulnerable end-users and increasing systemic risk.

conflicts.point: Whether pre-deployment gating and strict liability rules effectively deter flawed algorithmic deployment or merely erect bureaucratic barriers that delay critical care and legal aid.

positions.stance: Enforceable pre-market gates and strict liability are essential guardrails that prevent institutional collapse and protect human life and freedom.
Slow regulatory review and strict compliance gates externalize the cost of delay onto vulnerable populations, creating a silent body count of institutional stasis.

verdicts.conflict: Whether decentralized open-weight distribution improves safety and clinical outcomes through peer audit more effectively than centralized pre-market gatekeeping.
verdicts.rationale: Both sides present plausible systemic risks without sufficient longitudinal deployment data from high-stakes clinical and judicial settings. Accelerationists cite the theoretical speed of peer review, while safetyists highlight the absence of traceability and accountability when models fail.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Independent safety audits tracking clinical error rates across hospitals using open-weight versus proprietary models over a multi-year period would tip the balance.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-deployment gating and strict liability rules effectively deter flawed algorithmic deployment or merely erect bureaucratic barriers that delay critical care and legal aid.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position offers concrete liability mechanisms that courts can enforce, whereas the counterargument relies on broad assertions about corporate shielding without offering an alternative enforcement structure.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical proof that compliance gates systematically delay life-saving medical interventions more frequently than unvetted models cause fatal triage errors would alter this assessment.
